_readme: GAME CONTENT, DRAFT PENDING PRODUCER REVIEW (region and seal names, level bands, map rules). The region campaign: ten regions cover levels 1-100 in order; after them, POST-GAME regions (IsPostGame true: r11 Duskmeridian, unlocked by r10's boss) sit outside that band at a flat level 100 (MinLevel = MaxLevel = 100), grant no seal (BossRewardSealId empty: the cap is already at its peak), draw only post-game shapes (encounter-library.json PostGame), and may be played on Normal or Hard (the player's choice when an expedition starts, CampaignRules.StartRun; HardMode names the Hard shapes, elite shape and boss template; the same loot, plus Hard-only boss looks). RegionLibraryValidator checks them in a separate pass after the mainline band; --mode campaign keeps them out of its mainline tables and reports them in its own Post-game section. The player explores each region as a MAP of locations (wilds, dens, camps, trading posts, a pass, the boss's lair; open world TBD) over Stages expeditions; the node maps are the internal pacing model behind that map, never shown as a graph (each node also gets a location kind, a normalized map position and a label key from NodeMapGenerator.Place, for a spatial map UI). Expeditions: node maps generated by the runtime NodeMapGenerator from MapRules and a seed, Slay-the-Spire style: Paths walks over Lanes x (Layers - 1) rows, row 0 Battle, RestLayer all Rest (Camp: train one beast), the top a single Gate (stages before the last) or the region's Boss (the last stage); other nodes drawn by NodeWeights, Elite/Rest/Shop never following their own type, no Elite below EliteMinLayer, MinElites-MaxElites Elites and at most MaxShops Shops per map). Node level: MinLevel + floor(t x (MaxLevel - MinLevel) / T), t = stage x (Layers - 1) + row, T = Stages x (Layers - 1); Elites +EliteLevelOffset, Gates +GateLevelOffset, the Boss exactly MaxLevel. Battle nodes draw a shape by the region's ShapeWeights (encounter-library.json shapes); Elites and generated Gates use EliteShapeId; the Boss fields BossTemplateId (encounter-library.json Templates) and grants BossRewardSealId. Seals are key items: the beast level cap is the highest owned seal's LevelCap, or StartingLevelCap (first region max + LevelCapMargin). A region's own MapRules override the library's when its Layers is above 0. EARLY-REGION EASING (producer decision), per kind of fight: EasingShapeScales holds each ordinary shape's FULL discount (a scale on the stat multiplier; a shape not listed, including 'boss', is never eased) and each region's StageEasing, per stage, how much of it applies (1 = all, 0 = none; scale = 1 - weight x (1 - full)); CampaignRules.PlanFor with the run applies it to campaign battles only (the calibrated table and the balance simulator's calibration never see it). Validated: known shapes once each, scales in (0, 1]; StageEasing empty or one weight per stage in [0, 1], never rising, reaching 0 before it stops, mainline only. Since the typical-team calibration (Tooling/BalanceSim --mode typical) and adaptive assist (below), the no-gear typical-team need is mild (Tooling/BalanceSim --mode newplayer, docs/balance/new-player-report.md): only r01 keeps a small discount, fully faded out by its own last stage (StageEasing [1, 1, 1, 0]; r02 and r03 need none, StageEasing empty); the boss needs none anywhere, so 'boss' is not in EasingShapeScales and no region sets BossScale (docs/balance/tuning-log.md, 'Never-blocked targets'). BossScale (0 = none): a region's own scale for its boss in place of the shared 'boss' discount, when one is listed; mainline only, where the last stage is eased. ADAPTIVE ASSIST (producer decision, "assist + guidance"): each consecutive loss at the same campaign location eases that fight further, on top of any early-region easing (AssistStep, about -10% a loss, compounding; CampaignRules.LossesAt / RegionLibrary.AssistScaleFor), down to AssistFloorScales (same shape list as EasingShapeScales, 'boss' included: unlike the early-region easing, the floor DOES cover the boss), or a region's own AssistBossFloorScale for its boss in place of the shared 'boss' floor (r11 Duskmeridian Normal: its typical target is already lower than a mainline boss's, 35% not 75%, so the shared floor under-assists it). 0 or an empty AssistStep disables it everywhere; a shape or 'boss' not in AssistFloorScales is never assisted. Off on post-game Hard (RunDifficulty.Hard); resets on a win; rewards and XP never change. The floor is chosen so the WEAK owned-roster pick reaches about 70% for an ordinary fight or 60% for a region boss (Tooling/BalanceSim --mode assistfloor, docs/balance/tuning-log.md, "Never-blocked targets"). CampaignRules.PlanFor also shows the discount as EncounterPlan.AssistScale, for the preview's "the wilds ease a little" note. Validated by RegionLibraryValidator (the Editor importer Beast Craft/Data/Import Regions, the EditMode tests, Tooling/BalanceSim --mode campaign); paced by --mode campaign (docs/balance/campaign-pacing-report.md). See docs/design/progression-and-saves.md, 'Region campaign'. Region, seal and location text (region and seal DisplayName / Description; the map location names in location-names.json, resolved from each node's LabelKey by LocationNameTable) is DRAFT pending producer review, written to docs/design/content-bible.md. TUTORIAL REGIONS (TutorialRegions, kept out of Regions so the mainline band, the calibration and every campaign tool never see them): Hearthglen (r00, IsTutorial), the onboarding region a new game starts in, played once as one expedition over its authored FixedNodes (Type Story, Battle, Trial or Rest; Name; Level; TemplateId: an hg_* template with its own DifficultyOverride, never the table or the easing; PickStep 2 and 3 on the Trials; SceneId: a dialogue.json scene; Lane; Kind; Grants: consumables a Story hands over; OpenBoard: fought on the open board; AdaptiveElements: the enemies take the element neutral against the player) fought on BattlefieldRegionId's battlefields; clearing its last location unlocks r01 (docs/design/area-zero.md).

Seals.Description: A moss-furred standing stone from the heart of Verdant Hollow. Claiming it raises your binding limit.
A seal-stone that never quite cools, pried from the ridge of Emberreach. Claiming it raises your binding limit.
A seal-stone crusted with shells, raised from the drowned ruins of Tidefall. Claiming it raises your binding limit.
A seal-stone that whistles in the slightest breeze, taken from the crags of Stormcrag. Claiming it raises your binding limit.
A seal-stone laced with iron that rings when touched, freed from the Rustwood. Claiming it raises your binding limit.
A seal-stone rimed in frost that never melts, lifted from the ice of Frostmere. Claiming it raises your binding limit.
A seal-stone that crackles with static, taken from the highest spire of Thunderspire. Claiming it raises your binding limit.
A seal-stone wrapped in living roots, drawn from the heart of the Deepwild. Claiming it raises your binding limit.
A seal-stone of black volcanic glass, taken from the Cinder Throne. Claiming it lifts your binding limit to its peak.
The last seal-stone, set where fire meets water on the Worldcrown. Your bond is already whole; claiming it stems the Gloam at its source.

Regions.Description: A sun-dappled woodland of moss, ferns and old standing stones where every Beastbinder's journey begins. The Gloam is thin here, and the creatures it touches are more lost than fierce.
Ash-dusted ridges below a smouldering peak, where warm winds carry sparks and the rocks glow at dusk. Fire creatures bask on every ledge.
Sea caves and drowned ruins where the tide pours in like a waterfall twice a day. Cold currents from the north bring frost to the deepest pools.
Wind-cut crags above the cloud line, strung with rope bridges and nesting cliffs. The gales never stop, and neither do the creatures that ride them.
A forest of iron trees that rust red in the rain and ring like bells in the wind, rooted in stony ground rich with ore.
A frozen lake as wide as a sea, ringed by snowfields and pine. The ice sings at night, and something vast sleeps beneath it.
A forest of glassy spires that drink the lightning. The air hums, hair stands on end, and every storm leaves the rocks crackling.
The oldest, deepest forest, where trees grow as tall as towers and the undergrowth hums with life. Paths here move when no one is looking.
The volcanic heart of the land: rivers of lava, fields of black glass and a molten throne at the summit, held by the Cinder King.
The summit at the end of the Farwild, where fire and water pour from the same peak and the Gloam wells up between them. Only the strongest bonds reach it.

Beyond the Worldcrown the Gloam thins into an endless gold-and-violet evening, where radiant dawn and deep dusk share one sky. The eldest creatures of the Farwild gather here to test any bond whole enough to reach them.

TutorialRegions.Description: A sheltered vale below the tree line, where Verdant Hollow begins: warm hedgerows, an old mill, a shrine with a keeper who remembers the first Beastbinders. Only a faint shimmer at the far hedge says the Gloam is near.
